title: Akaroa Harbour Atlas
outcome: One harbour, five small systems: the water, wastewater, power and roads around Akaroa, on one map
summary: An interactive atlas of Akaroa Harbour, the crater of an extinct volcano with Akaroa, Takamātua, Duvauchelle, Wainui, Tikao Bay and Ōnuku around it. Each settlement has its own pipes, pumps and plants, all run from Christchurch and all reached by one state highway. The atlas maps them from the council's open GIS and OpenStreetMap, with the projects and decisions that will shape the harbour for decades.

stats.label: Council projects in train around the harbour

sections.head: Small systems, big decisions
sections.body: Akaroa's water, wastewater, power and road each have their own story, spread across council reports, consent decisions and news coverage. The sewage plant sits on Takapūneke and discharges to the harbour under a consent that runs out in 2030, the 1887 Main Wharf is being rebuilt, and SH75 is the only sealed way in. It is hard to see how any of it fits together.

sections.head: See the harbour as one place
sections.body: Put every network on the same 3D map of the harbour, explain each in plain language with its sources, and show what is being built and decided alongside what was proposed before and didn't go ahead.

sections.head: A story in eight pages, and a map for each system
sections.body: An eight-page story walks from the one road in to the water supply, the wastewater question, Orion's single line, Takapūneke, the wharf and the marine reserve. Tabs open each system with its own key: water, wastewater, power, roads, ports, landmarks, public land, the peninsula, history and the council's capital programme. Network data is the council's public GIS as published in November 2026, with OpenStreetMap for power and reserves and LINZ for terrain and aerials. It is a map for understanding, not for digging.
